verdict.rationale: Pulumi's own DIY backend lets you keep stack state in object storage you manage (S3, Azure Blob, GCS), and the platform is open source with infrastructure defined as code in standard languages, which gives meaningful data control and portability. However, the evidence never documents an explicit export of all data (state, history, secrets, config) from Pulumi Cloud, nor states that the state format is open. missing for 10: documented full-account or stack export command, explicit open/documented state file format, documented migration path off Pulumi Cloud, coverage of history/secrets/ESC data export, independent hands-on corroboration of leaving.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can export all of my data in open formats and leave

citations.quote: DIY backend: a “Do It Yourself” backend that stores state in an object store you manage—AWS S3, Azure Blob Storage, Google Cloud Storage
Pulumi is an open source platform for building, deploying, and managing cloud infrastructure using your favorite programming languages.
The Pulumi Cloud REST API is used by the Pulumi CLI to query and interact with state information, history, stack tags, etc.
